_comment: Schema reference for the per-plugin config files. You do not run this file —
run config.mock.json / config.mosip.json / config.sunbird.json, which are
tracked alongside it, and put your credentials in config.local.json (copy
Almost every field has an environment override that wins over both files;
the README's 'Env overrides' table is the complete list. The exceptions —
no env override at all, so a container must mount the config file to change
them — are run.modules, run.known_issues, and every plans[] field except
Nothing here is worth guessing at: ./run-all.sh -c <config> --check prints
the fully resolved result, runs nothing, and needs no suite up.
//conformance: The OpenID Conformance Suite instance the conformance surface drives.
base_url    where the suite is             (env CONFORMANCE_BASE_URL)
tls_verify  false for the suite's self-signed local cert
token       bearer token, ONLY for a suite instance that requires auth.
Leave empty for the local/prebuilt suite, which does not.
A credential — set it via the env var or config.local.json,
never in a tracked file.       (env CONFORMANCE_TOKEN)
//plans: The conformance plans ONE run executes, in order. Each entry is a separate
suite plan: its own variant and its own config_file (client + jwks), so two
entries mean two client/key sets. The api and e2e surfaces still run once,
and every plan's modules land in the same consolidated report under its own
profile/modules/filter/skip/known_issues are optional per plan and fall back
to the same-named run.* field. profile=smoke reads data/conformance/<name>.smoke.json,
so a plan with no profile file of its own needs profile=full here.
config_file paths are secrets-adjacent (the file holds the private jwks):
keep them out of this tracked file if they differ per machine — an overlay's
plans[] merges entry-by-entry, so config.local.json can list just the
config_file of each. Env: PLAN_1_CONFIG_PATH, PLAN_2_CONFIG_PATH, …
(PLAN_CONFIG_PATH without an index only works for a single-plan config).
The legacy singular "plan": {...} block still works and is read as a
one-entry plans list; setting both is an error.

plans.name: oidcc-test-plan
//selection: The four keys below are the per-plan module selection. All optional:
each falls back to the same-named run.* field, so delete them to run
the profile as-is. They are shown here because prose is not enough to
guess known_issues' element shape.
Order: modules (or profile) picks a list -> filter narrows it -> skip
and known_issues subtract from it.
modules REPLACES the profile rather than narrowing it: set it and
profile is never consulted (--check prints 'modules N explicitly
listed (profile ignored)'). A name that is not in the plan still gets
a report row, so a typo is visible instead of silently selecting less.
skip and known_issues do not run the module but still report it — in
the Skipped and Known buckets respectively, neither of which affects
the Failed count or the exit code. They subtract from whatever was
already selected, so naming a module the plan never selected is a
silent no-op.

//esignet: The eSignet deployment under test — every surface drives this one.
provider    which plugin is deployed: mock|mosip|sunbird
auth_factor which ACR to pick when the flow offers a choice
tls_verify  certificate verification for eSignet. Defaults to TRUE and
should stay there: this connection carries the test
identity, its OTP and its password. It is deliberately
separate from conformance.tls_verify, which is false only
for the suite's self-signed localhost cert. Set false only
for a deployment with a self-signed cert of its own.

//selection: Run-wide module selection. Every plans[] entry falls back to these, so
set them here for a one-plan config and per plan when two plans want
different module sets. Same precedence as documented in plans[] above.
modules       explicit allow-list; replaces profile entirely.
profile       smoke = data/conformance/<plan name>.smoke.json, full = every
module the plan declares.            (env TEST_PROFILE)
filter        regex over whatever modules/profile produced.
(env TEST_RUN)
skip          not run -> Skipped bucket.           (env SKIP_MODULES)
known_issues  not run -> Known bucket, shown with its reason.
filter applies AFTER the list is chosen: with profile=smoke it filters
INSIDE the smoke list, not across the plan. To regex over a plan's full
module set, set profile=full as well.
modules and known_issues have no env override, and no plans[] field has
one beyond name/config_file (PLAN_<n>_NAME, PLAN_<n>_CONFIG_PATH) — a
container that needs to change the rest must mount the config file itself.
Module names come from the suite when the plan is created, so they
track SUITE_IMAGE_TAG: run once with profile=full and read the report
to see the real names for a plan.
Preview all of this without running anything:
./run-all.sh -c <config> --check
//pacing: poll_interval_seconds  how often to poll the suite for a module's
timeout_seconds        per-module ceiling; a module still WAITING at
the end is reported as a timeout, not a pass.
fail_fast              stop the WHOLE run on the first failure —
report_dir             where the HTML + .json sidecar are written.
//debug_show_secrets: Local debugging only. Leaves the captured eSignet wire trace unredacted in
the report and its sidecar JSON — request/response bodies, URLs, cookies and
headers exactly as they went over the wire, including OTPs, passwords,
identity values and bearer tokens. The report carries a red warning banner
when this is on. Never leave it on for a run CI archives.
The configuration panel and the suite plan config stay masked either way.
